text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deception troubles Canadian Defence Minister David Collenette: Former U..S officer denies giving order to kill while in Canadian uniform.
- Mideast stakes high at talks: Leaders to focus on peace process.
- Taliban extremism horrifies Pakistan: Other neighbours of Afghanistan are deeply wary of rebel Islamic group.
- Welfare recipients struggle with cuts: Demand for food banks increases.
- Tension rises in Hebron: Jewish pilgrims stream into divided city for massive rally.
- New Democratic Party returns to power in Yukon.
- Economy barrels ahead: GDP growth of 0.5 percent in July led by manufacturing sector's biggest gain in almost a decade.
- Higher bid for Silcorp allowed to lapse: Couche-Tard raised bid on Friday.
- Lewiscraft gets court protection from its creditors: Retailer another victim of U.S. invasion.
- Feel-good factor feeds British boom: John Major's Tories are hoping to ride a wave of economic resurgence back into No. 10 Downing Street.

- Bigger Employment Insurance surplus sought: Bureaucrats tell Paul Martin not to cave in to provinces and cut Employment Insurance premiums because a C$15-billion buffer against the next recession needs to be built.

- Milk store battle gets hotter with Silcorp's purchase of Becker Milk Co Ltd: Takeover prey Silcorp has beaten its predator, Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc, in a bidding war for corner-store rival Becker's.
